title: feat(automation): triggers and the inbound hook dispatch by slot, so each package's flow of a shared name is armed and reached by its own hook
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-support-ai"} -->
_Requested by **Yibo Wang** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwB?thread=cmsg_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwBACaR2yPzyA9bofAfNpzFDY)_

Part of #31696

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：两个包共用一个流程名时，四种触发器（记录变更、定时、相对时间、入站钩子）按槽位各自武装、各自触发本包的流程，不再一律拒绝。第二个持有者到来时先撤销裸名任务，再武装两个限定任务（`flow-schedule:包/名`），反向同理；撤销滞后期间旧任务的触发不运行，所以每个槽位每个窗口只触发一次。入站钩子：限定地址 `/automation/hooks/:ns/:flowName/:hookId` 运行该命名空间的槽位并用该包的密钥校验；共享名的裸地址不指向任何一个流程，回答这扇匿名门统一的 401（与改前相同），原因 `shared-name` 和两个持有包只写服务器日志。
- 为什么改：这是 ADR-0150 子卡 B（flow）的 PR-2，按席位裁定 Q3 = A、Q4 = A 执行。PR-1a/1b 已让引擎和凭据通道按槽位运行，但触发器仍按名绑定，所以共享名的流程只能手动调用。
- 风险与回滚：名称只有一个持有者时，绑定、任务名、分发键、运行和钩子回答都与改前相同（各有 CONTROL 钉）。没有收窄：共享名下原来不武装，钩子原来统一 401，现在裸地址仍是 401。D5 的 409 不适用于这扇匿名门：它的回答从不透露某个流程名是否存在、装了哪些包。回滚直接 revert。
- 先看：`engine.ts` 的 `activateFlowTrigger`、`triggerRun`、`flowDispatchHolder`、`inboundHookSlot`；`trigger-api/src/plugin.ts` 的 `answerInboundHookSlot`；`runtime/src/domains/automation-hooks.ts` 的限定地址分支。
- 两分钟验证：`cd packages/services/service-automation && npx vitest run src/flow-triggers-per-slot.test.ts`（应为 10 条全部通过），以及 `cd packages/triggers/trigger-schedule && npx vitest run src/schedule-slot-rearm.test.ts`（3 条）。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

Narrowing: no
Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none in this PR — carried to PR-3. The `skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md` inbound-hook line (a name two packages ship is posted to `hooks/<namespace>/…` per package; the bare path gets the one refusal) applies only to a name two packages hold, so it rides PR-3 with the `subflow` parenthetical carried from #32239 and #32302, where the skills text for the flow family lands once. No skill text teaches anything this PR changes for a name one package holds.

ADR-0150 child B (flow), **PR-2** of the card's parts, after PR-1a (#32239) and PR-1b (#32302). PR-3 adds the other `/automation` doors, the namespace switch, dogfood and `Fixes`.

## New public names

- `AutomationEngine.inboundHookSlot(flowName, address?)` (`@objectstack/service-automation`): which slot's hook a hook address reaches. `undefined` for a name that is no slot key and that no two packages hold.
- `AutomationEngine.flowDispatchHolder(name)`: its answer gains an optional `name` member, given only for a slot key.
- `ApiTrigger.refuseUnknownFlow(flowName)` and `ApiTrigger.refuseSharedName(flowName, holders)` (the one refusal, cause `shared-name` logged with the holders) (`@objectstack/trigger-api`).
- The `trigger-api` service object gains `handleInboundSlotHook(request, { key, hookId })` beside `handleInboundHook`. It is not on the `ITriggerApiService` contract; only the hosted face calls it.
- The optional `name` member on `ScheduleDispatchLedger.flowDispatchHolder` and `FlowDispatchClaimSurface.flowDispatchHolder` (`@objectstack/trigger-schedule`).

## Measured on main (`b2c0202f`) before the change

For a flow name two packages hold:

| Path | On main | `premise_still_valid` |
|:--|:--|:--|
| record-change, schedule, time-relative, api (arming) | `activateFlowTrigger` declined every slot of the name (`isSharedFlowKey`), one warning per slot; no trigger was handed either slot | true |
| bare hook `/automation/hooks/:flowName/:hookId` | no hook is armed under the bare name, so the uniform `401 INVALID_SIGNATURE` (`unknown-flow`) | true |
| qualified hook, namespace | `packagedFlowOwner(name)` answers none for a bare shared name, so the address is unadmitted: the same `401` | true |
| qualified hook, `_env` | admitted (no owner), then no hook under the bare name: the same `401` | true |

A name one package holds was armed under its bare name on every trigger, and that is unchanged.

## What changes

- **`engine.ts`**
  - `activateFlowTrigger` arms a slot of a shared name under its key. It keeps declining only the M1 state: one slot left while the registry holds the name twice (the other body refused). That slot still holds the bare key, which would read as the name's one holder.
  - `triggerRun(armedKey)` is the run a trigger fires. It fires the slot it armed, at whatever key the slot holds now, and never re-resolves the bare name. If the slot's key moved and its old binding was released, it runs nothing: that is an event the released binding delivered before its cancel landed, and the binding under the new key fires it once. A slot of an unshared name runs through `execute` exactly as before. For a slot of a shared name the run's `params.flowName` is the flow's name, not the key.
  - `flowDispatchHolder(slotKey)` answers `{ packageId: <slot's package>, claimBare: false, name }`. The key it spells (`schedule:PACKAGE:NAME:WINDOW`) is the key the same slot claimed while it held the name alone, so a window the re-arm straddles is claimed once.
  - `inboundHookSlot(flowName, address?)`:
    - a slot-key spelling answers `unadmitted`;
    - a bare shared name answers `refused` with every holder;
    - a qualified shared name answers `served` with the key of the one slot whose package the namespace owns (`_env`: the slot no package holds), else `unadmitted`;
    - anything else answers `undefined`.
  - The re-arm order is the existing `moveFlowRecords`: every moved key is deactivated before any is activated.
- **`trigger-schedule`**: the schedule and time-relative triggers spell the dispatch key with `holder.name ?? flowName`. Job names follow the binding's key, so `flow-schedule:NAME` becomes `flow-schedule:PACKAGE/NAME` per slot.
- **`trigger-record-change`**: no change. It binds and fires by the key the engine hands it.
- **`trigger-api`**:
  - The self-hosted mount asks `inboundHookSlot` on both routes. A served slot is handled by the same door under its key. An unadmitted address gets the one refusal (`unadmitted-address`, or `unknown-flow` for a bare slot key). A refused bare name (a name two packages hold) gets the same one refusal, its cause `shared-name` and the holders logged only.
  - The `trigger-api` member (`handleInboundHook`, which the hosted bare route calls) answers a bare shared name with the same one refusal and refuses a name carrying `/` as an unknown flow, so it never serves a slot key that the path carried. Its new `handleInboundSlotHook` serves only a key that the hosted face's engine routed.
- **`runtime` (`automation-hooks.ts`)**:
  - On the qualified route, the hosted face asks the request kernel's `inboundHookSlot` and serves a routed slot through `handleInboundSlotHook`. An address no slot answers gets the one refusal. A trigger with no slot door is refused, never served by name.
  - The bare route is unchanged: it reads no service before the member, so the #22773 condition-2 pin stands.
- **`core`**: no change. ADR-0150 D5's `409` naming the holders does not apply to this anonymous door, whose answer never says whether a flow name exists or which packages are installed.
- **Changeset**: `.changeset/31696-triggers-hook-by-slot.md` (patch on the four packages, ADR-0087 `not-required`).
- **`scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`**: the new dogfood file's credential-store double opens `update` / `delete` with the engine dispatch predicates and bounds `find` by `limit`; the pinned ledger records its two new rows (`--write`).

## Rulings, item by item

1. Each trigger dispatches the slot that armed it, never the bare name at fire time. One-holder CONTROL pins: the engine (`flow-triggers-per-slot.test.ts`), the schedule job and key (`schedule-slot-rearm.test.ts`), the hook on both faces, and the dogfood file.
2. Q3 = A: `flow-schedule:NAME` while one package holds the name, `flow-schedule:PACKAGE/NAME` per slot. The bare job is cancelled before the qualified jobs are armed, and the reverse when the second holder leaves. Exactly once in each direction is pinned with the real `ScheduleTrigger` over a job service whose cancels land late.
3. Hook: the qualified hook runs its namespace's slot, verified with that slot's secret read through the #32302 channel (the end-to-end pin uses the real `FlowCredentialChannel`). Re-ruled by the seat: the bare hook of a shared name answers the door's one refusal (401) once the body is read, on both faces; the cause (`shared-name`) and both holders go to the server log only. Main already answered 401 there, so this is no narrowing.
4. Q4 = A: an environment row over a shared name overlays neither holder. Both packages' bodies arm their triggers, and one warning names both packages and the row. The warning is #32239's; the arming is new here.
5. Disabled: a slot switched off (`toggleFlowSlot`) arms nothing and fires nothing, and the other holder's binding stands. Its qualified hook still routes to its slot, whose hook is not armed, so the trigger answers it as it answers a disabled flow's (401). Finding, outside this PR's scope and reported on the card, of #32183's class (holders judged over the served set): `SchemaRegistry.disablePackage` keeps the package among the name's package-scoped holders, so the resolver still refuses the bare name; once that package's slot is withdrawn the other is the M1 lone-shared slot and stays declined, and its bare hook gets the one refusal (`shared-name` logged). Item 5 is therefore pinned through the slot switch.
6. `bare-name-one-holder.ts` and the `/automation` doors other than the hook are untouched. plugin-approvals is untouched.

## Pins and ablations

All 15 ablations ran through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` on the committed tree (B13 and B14 retired with the core helper this round reverted). Each went red and each was restored to HEAD (`git diff HEAD` empty).

| # | Mutation | Pin that went red |
|:--|:--|:--|
| B1 | `triggerRun` drops no stale event (released binding still runs) | `flow-triggers-per-slot` "released by a re-arm" (1 failed) |
| B2 | `activateFlowTrigger` declines every shared slot again (main's rule) | `flow-triggers-per-slot` (5 of 10 failed) |
| B3 | a shared slot's run re-resolves the bare name | "never re-resolves" (1 failed) |
| B4 | `flowDispatchHolder` gives no slot answer | "dispatch key is spelled" (1 failed) |
| B5 | time-relative key spelled with the binding key, not `holder.name` | `time-relative-trigger` "slot bound under its key" (1 failed) |
| B6 | schedule key spelled with the binding key | `schedule-slot-rearm` (2 of 3 failed) |
| B7 | `inboundHookSlot` admits a slot-key spelling | "reach no hook" (1 failed) |
| B8 | a bare shared hook name is not refused | "bare address is refused" (1 failed) |
| B9 | `params.flowName` keeps the slot key | "reads the flow's name" (1 failed) |
| B10 | the self-hosted bare route skips slot routing | `inbound-hook-member` "the bare hook answers the one refusal…" (1 failed: no `shared-name` cause) |
| B11 | hosted face hands the slot door the bare name, not the key | `automation-hooks` "reaches its namespace" (1 failed) |
| B12 | hosted face serves by name when the slot door is missing | `automation-hooks` "a trigger with no slot door … is refused" (1 failed) |
| B15 | the M1 lone-shared slot is armed | `flow-slots-per-package` "[M1, PR-2]" (1 failed) |
| B16 | the bare shared hook answers a `409` naming the holders | `inbound-hook-member` "the bare hook answers the one refusal…" (1 failed) |
| B17 | the bare shared hook's refusal logs no cause | the same pin (1 failed) |
